newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker on softer U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker on softer U.S. market.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Monday, softening in tandem with U.S. Treasuries, as investors in both markets took profits after Friday's unexpected rally, analysts said.

"I think we're mainly, as usual, tracking the U.S. a little bit weaker. There's no significant stories in Canada today," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed-income analyst with TD Securities Inc. "The rally that we saw on Friday, at the time it felt like it was overdone."
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.37 to C$113.91 to yield 6.896 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.80 percent. The spread between the bonds was 10 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied sharply on Friday as traders scrambled to cover short positions after the release of key employment data in both countries. This morning, traders in both countries took profits on Friday's rally, which saw the Canadian 30-year bond close up C$1.82.
Canadian housing starts and capacity utilization data out this morning were largely in line with expectations and had little impact on the bond market, analysts said.
"I think we're going to continue basically to track the U.S. There's no events scheduled that I'm aware of that we expect will have a signifcant impact on the market," said TD's Bendiksrud.
The Province of Ontario on Monday set C$500 million of 7.6 percent bonds due June 2, 2027 in financial markets. The offering was a reopening of a previous issue.

The bond was priced at C$106.544 to yield 7.071 percent, 20.5 basis points over the Government of Canada 8.0 percent bond due June, 2023. The bonds will pay interest on December 2 and June 2. The issue will be delivered on June 16.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.33 to C$106.24 to yield 6.394 percent while the U.S. 10-year fell 5/32 to 6.51 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 12 basis points from 14 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.90 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.07 percent.
